# A source-smoothed full Stein inverse with a finite random action

This is an internal mathematical construction for the N687 opening in frozen S3 Sections 17–18. It is not the requested g-only polylogarithmic sampler. The sharp scalar inverse was independently derived by the authorised helper; the vector gauge and integration below are the main trajectory's construction. Gaussian second quantization, Hermite calculus, and Gaussian density Taylor bounds are standard instruments. External priority has not been established.

## 1. Statement, with the actual access boundary

Fix any physical dimension d, 0<kappa<1, and a=sqrt(1-kappa²). On independent standard Gaussian G,Z in R^d consider the exact affine Gaussian source

    h(G)=kappa G, K=kappa I, psi=aZ, Jpsi=aI,
    X=kappa G+aZ ~ N(0,I).

For a symmetric matrix field R in L2(gamma_(2d); Frobenius), let P_a^G be source-only Gaussian OU smoothing. There exist u and J such that

    delta_Z J=u,                    E_Z u=0,
    sym[kappa(D_G u)^T+a(D_Z u)^T+aJ] = -P_a^G R.       (1)

The norms ||u||_2, ||D_Zu||_2, ||kappa D_Gu||_2, and ||J||_2 have bounds depending on kappa,a but on neither d nor chaos degree. The smoothing is explicit and cannot be deleted: even in d=1 the unsmoothed inverse is unbounded on L2. Source-only P_rho restores bounded inversion precisely when rho<=a in that scalar problem.

More than an existence inverse is available. One conditional-unbiased action for u uses one value of R applied to a Gaussian vector, a fixed number of Gaussian vectors/scalars, and O(d) surrounding vector arithmetic. If a full R matrix is returned, its multiplication costs O(d²). The program has no random loop or unbounded query count. Its exact second moment is

    E||Uhat||² = pi²/(8a²) E||R(G,Z)||_F².              (2)

If ||R||op<=b everywhere, Uhat is convex-order dominated by N(0,pi² b²/(8a²) I). An unbiased noisy action A(y;v) can replace the R(y)v evaluation: the conditional mean remains u, and the actual action's second moment must replace the right side of (2).

The original oracle supplies g values, not R values or actions. This distinction is load-bearing. In particular, raw Dg at an acquired point is not a free value-query action. Frozen S4 gives exact bounded actions for smoothed heat Hessians and Stein resolvents; obtaining the complete nonlinear residual from those actions is a remaining task.

# An actual g-value implementation on the conservative stress family

This is a validation of the law-update mechanism, not a universal sampler or an advantage claim. An equally informed ordinary competitor uses g(0) to learn the mean of this known family and adds Gaussian noise, with one query.

Let the supplied family parameters kappa,eta,k be positive, kappa+eta<1, and let an unknown constant m enter the genuine conservative source

    g(x)=m+kappa x+eta sin(kx)/k,
    F(x)=m x+kappa x²/2-eta cos(kx)/k².

Its mean is m. Put a=sqrt(1-kappa²) and X=g(G)+aZ. The actual Stein residual is the R_k from CORE_THEOREM.md (11), with delta=eta. Define

    C_omega(x)=exp[kappa² omega²/(2a²)] cos(omega x/a),
    w(t)=exp[-k²(1-t²)/2].

Because P_a C_omega=cos(omega x), the exact source preimage R0 is

    R0(x)=kappa eta C_k(x)
       + integral_0^1 w(t){kappa eta C_(kt)(x)
             +eta²[C_(k(1+t))(x)+C_(k(1-t))(x)]/2}dt.   (1)

This preimage is constructed, not assumed. Draw a single uniform T in [0,1] and replace the integral in (1) by its integrand at T, obtaining Rhat0(x). It is conditionally unbiased and has deterministic magnitude bound

    |Rhat0(x)|<=b=2kappa eta E_k+eta² E_(2k),
    E_v=exp[kappa²v²/(2a²)].                           (2)

No derivative or potential value is needed to evaluate a cosine. For any v,

    cos(kv)=k{g(v+pi/(2k))-g(v-pi/(2k))-kappa pi/k}
                                                          /(2eta).  (3)

There are four cosines in Rhat0 and hence eight original g-value calls. Generate Y_G,V as in CORE_THEOREM.md and return

    g(G)+aZ-pi/(2sqrt(2)a) Rhat0(Y_G)V+tau N.           (4)

The total is nine g queries on every execution, with no stochastic loop. The uniform T is generated by the first coordinate of a three-dimensional Gaussian divided by its radius and mapped affinely to [0,1]. All unknown constant offsets cancel in (3).

For exact scalar formulas the theorem of CORE_THEOREM.md Section 8 and the actual second-moment bound (2) give

    TV(Law(output),N(m,(1+tau²)))
      <= H(tau)[A eta b+B b²]+phi(1)c² b²/tau²,        (5)

with the constants defined there. Thus for fixed kappa,k,tau this is a positive, original-value-only nonlinear update with error O(eta²), whereas its coefficient perturbation and initial Stein residual are O(eta). The entire implemented randomness, including the random residual action, is in

statement: At X=kappa G+aZ,a=sqrt(1-kappa^2),0<kappa<1, every symmetric Frobenius-L2 residual R has a controlled full inverse of -P_a^G R in the strict noise-divergence gauge. A finite one-residual-action program has conditional mean u and exact energy pi^2||R||_2^2/(8a^2). Scalar source-only P_rho gives bounded inversion iff rho<=a; larger rho and unsmoothed inversion are unbounded.
